assertions.text: Repository development practice: docs/bun.md instructs contributors to default to Bun (bun test, bun install, Bun.file, Bun.serve) and avoid Node/dotenv/express equivalents; docs/code-convention.md mandates kebab-case files, named exports only, _-prefixed private members, and layered dependency direction (agent stays generic; adapters live in community/).

The OpenAI provider defaults to temperature 0 and top_p 0, merges caller options last, and works with any OpenAI-compatible endpoint; thinking content is dropped when converting messages to OpenAI wire format.
The stack uses TypeScript strict/ESM on the Bun runtime, Zod for schemas, the OpenAI SDK, Ink with React 19 for the TUI, Commander for the CLI, and gray-matter plus yaml for skills parsing.

Repository development practice: docs/bun.md instructs contributors to default to Bun (bun test, bun install, Bun.file, Bun.serve) and avoid Node/dotenv/express equivalents; docs/code-convention.md mandates kebab-case files, named exports only, _-prefixed private members, and layered dependency direction (agent stays generic; adapters live in community/).
The foundation layer provides three core primitives: a Model abstraction over LLM providers, a single Message transcript type, and Tool definitions with execution plumbing.
The agent loop is ReAct-style: it maintains conversation state, orchestrates think-act-observe steps, invokes tool calls in parallel, and feeds observations back into the next reasoning step.
The CLI stores configuration in ~/.helixent/config.yaml and offers subcommands including 'helixent config model list', 'add', 'remove <model_name>', and 'set-default <model_name>'.
If an AGENTS.md file exists at the repository root, it is automatically picked up as project guidance, serving as long-term project memory.

The OpenAI provider defaults to temperature 0 and top_p 0, merges caller options last, and works with any OpenAI-compatible endpoint; thinking content is dropped when converting messages to OpenAI wire format.

The codebase is organized into three layers plus a community area: src/foundation (core primitives), src/agent (agent loop), src/coding (coding agent), and src/community (third-party integrations such as OpenAI).

Bun was chosen over Node for its native async/await concurrency, faster HTTP/filesystem/cold-start performance, single-file compiled executables via 'bun build --compile', and bundled test runner, bundler, and TypeScript support.

Repository development practice: all pushes and pull requests run 'bun run check' in GitHub Actions, local commits are gated by a pre-commit hook running the same check, and contributors build with bun install / bun run dev / bun run build:bin producing dist/bin/helixent.
Sub-agents, multi-agent teams, print mode, and file-based sessioning appear on the roadmap, suggesting these capabilities are planned rather than shipped in this version.

Skills in the standard agentskills.io format are discovered from ~/.agents/skills, ~/.helixent/skills, and the project's .agents/skills and .helixent/skills directories; duplicate skill names across folders are allowed.

A middleware system lets extensions observe and mutate agent behavior at eight lifecycle hooks (beforeAgentRun/afterAgentRun, beforeAgentStep/afterAgentStep, beforeModel/afterModel, beforeToolUse/afterToolUse), invoked sequentially in array order; hooks may return a partial update to merge or void.

The coding agent ships practical developer tools such as bash, read_file, write_file, str_replace, list_files, glob_search, grep_search, apply_patch, file_info, mkdir, and move_path, plus a todo-list-based plan mode.
The agent loop supports human-in-the-loop approval of tool calls, listed as a key feature of the middleware-ready loop.

Programmatic use is via createCodingAgent({ model }) from 'helixent/coding' and OpenAIModelProvider from 'helixent/community/openai'; agents expose a stream() method yielding messages whose content segments include thinking, text, and tool_use types.
Helixent is described as a coding agent comprising an agent loop, a coding-focused agent layer, and a CLI, distributed as the npm package 'helixent'.
The foundation layer provides three core primitives: a Model abstraction over LLM providers, a single Message transcript type, and Tool definitions with execution plumbing.

The OpenAI provider defaults to temperature 0 and top_p 0, merges caller options last, and works with any OpenAI-compatible endpoint; thinking content is dropped when converting messages to OpenAI wire format.

The ModelProvider contract requires invoke(params) returning Promise<AssistantMessage> and stream(params) returning an AsyncGenerator of AssistantMessage; params bundle model, messages, optional tools, provider options, and an AbortSignal.
